authorization: Ray, 2026-09-23 (same authorization as TECNO OTA probe)
method: protobuf check-in with synthetic identifiers, no IMEI

identity_fields.imei: OMITTED — not required, avoids GSMA-space collision

device_description.note: Infinix uses 'Infinix' as both oem and device prefix; itel uses 'Itel' as oem but 'itel' (lowercase) as device prefix

side_effects: each probe causes Google to allocate an ephemeral device registration (androidId). This is inherent to the check-in protocol with id=0 and was disclosed to Ray.

fields.has_update: whether the SYNTHETIC fingerprint submitted in this probe is behind the build Google offers for that model+region. The submitted fingerprints use placeholder incrementals from prober configs, NOT real device builds. This field describes our request, NOT any real device population. Do not report the ratio as a measurement of fleet update status.
fields.update_title: the build Google currently offers for this model+region. This is the durable finding — a freshness signal showing what firmware is live at the distribution point right now.
fields.update_url: OTA package URL — NON-DURABLE POINTER, likely signed/session-bound, may not resolve later. Recorded as metadata, NOT fetched.
fields.update_description: HTML description of the update (truncated to 500 chars)
fields.unexpected_update_fields: update_* field names in the response not in our extract list — typically Google Play client config knobs, not OTA metadata

stripped_fields: update_token — session-scoped bearer token, credential, never stored
androidId — ephemeral registration ID minted by Google per probe, not a device identity
notes: Extends the TECNO OTA probe to Infinix and itel brands
These brands have NO ASPL data from security.tecno.com — this is the first freshness signal for them
IMEI deliberately omitted from all requests
update_url may expire — same treatment as FRBox expired links
If any response shape differs from the baseline, it is flagged in unexpected_update_fields
